_: Kill-check for asc-09wx.14 stage G3: one gate at a time across sessions. A lock that is broken too eagerly puts two suites back on one machine -- the load the cut exists to remove -- and one that is broken too rarely turns a stale lock into a commit that never happens, so the mutants below are one per direction plus the two bookkeeping rules. Every killer was FOUND, not guessed: each mutant was planted in the working tree and its killing test file run with --reporter=json, and the failing names were read off assertionResults. Measured 2026-10-13. L4 and L5 share a killer deliberately -- the wait being recorded at all, and the gate not running while another session holds the lock, are the two halves of the same assertion. NOTE for anyone adding a mutant here: `acquire` BLOCKS, so a mutant that disables an unblocking rule makes its killer wait rather than fail -- no timeout exists in scripts/mutate.mjs. Every test of an unblocking rule therefore releases the lock from a helper process as an escape hatch, and any new killer of that kind needs one too, or the mutation run hangs instead of going red.
